authority: Framework course-long fluency map. It is separate from Intro/Review/Mastery and owns when each Warm-Up lane introduces, expands, and maintains content.
question_structure_exception: Warm-Ups are explicitly excluded from the universal Question Structure requirement. Keep the four stable jobs concise and routine-driven while maintaining mathematical quality.

daily_design.Q1 Solve / Equation Fluency: Normally a 2-equation mini-set. Three equations are allowed when all are very short one-step retrieval; one equation is allowed when the method is substantially longer. Never introduce a solve type earlier than the current section row/unit ceiling. Across the three section days, mix older types with the newly introduced type rather than making every equation the newest type.
daily_design.Q2 Diamond / Factoring Pattern: Normally one diamond/product-sum/factoring-pattern job per day. Vary which cells are known when mathematically useful. Build speed and structure recognition without turning the lane into a second full factoring lesson.
daily_design.Q3 Skill Review: Normally one short review job; a 2-3 item mini-set is allowed only when every item serves the same narrow prerequisite/fluency purpose. Use the listed section theme as a planned prerequisite runway, not random review.
daily_design.Q4 Challenge: One short reasoning job. Across a section's three days, vary the thinking when useful: pattern, explain, compare, error analysis, representation, generalize, model, or critique. Challenge means thinking, not uglier arithmetic.

solve_rule: Older solving types remain mixed after harder types are introduced; the lane becomes cumulative rather than replacing old skills. Difficulty comes from method choice and fluency, not coefficient inflation.

solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 1: One-step fluency, then simple two-step near the end. No distribution-to-solve, no multi-step simplify-first equations, and no variables on both sides in the Solve lane.
solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 2: Strengthen two-step; add combining like terms, distribution, and one-sided multi-step. Only a very simple variables-on-both-sides preview late in Unit 2.
solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 3: Finish the full linear-equation progression: variables on both sides, distribution/like terms, then reasonable rational/fraction coefficients. End with a cumulative full linear mix.
solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 4: Maintain full linear solving. Do not keep making coefficients or steps harder merely because the course is later.
solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 5: Maintain full linear solving while the conceptual course shifts toward factoring/quadratics.
solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 6: Keep linear retrieval and add quadratic solving methods only after each method has been taught.
solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 7: Cumulative linear/quadratic solving. No logarithmic/exponential-equation solving is introduced.
solve_unit_ceiling.Unit 8: Representative cumulative Algebra solving with linear/quadratic method choice; prioritize fluency and judgment over maximal complexity.

diamond_rule: Progress from number product-sum reasoning to signed factor-pair fluency, then connect that structure to trinomial/special-pattern factoring and maintain it.

diamond_unit_progression.Unit 3: Larger/mixed signed product-sum fluency; maintain speed and accuracy.
diamond_unit_progression.Unit 4: Bridge numeric product-sum thinking into monic trinomial structure near the end of the Unit.
diamond_unit_progression.Unit 5: Use the lane for actual factoring fluency and special patterns as those are taught.
diamond_unit_progression.Units 6-8: Maintain mixed factoring patterns so factoring remains available as a tool.

skill_review_rule: Rotate foundations and useful prerequisites intentionally. The lane may preteach an upcoming prerequisite, but should not become a second lesson on unreached content. For fraction/integer fluency, encourage trying without a calculator first while clearly allowing calculator use when needed.
challenge_rule: Short reasoning/pattern/generalization/error analysis/representation/nonroutine work; not merely uglier arithmetic. Everyone may attempt it; full completion is not required.
